descriptionChirho: Stative or intransitive physical desolation of land, cities, or persons — Qal stative/participle and Nifal passive describing a state of ruin or devastation (Arabic خَرِبَ/مُقْفِرَة, Korean 황폐한, Swahili ukiwa/kuharibika).

Psychological shock, horror, or astonishment at something terrible — Qal, Nifal, Hitpael, and Piel forms expressing the emotional reaction of being stunned or aghast (Arabic يَدْهَشُ/يَتَحَيَّرُ, Korean 놀라다, Swahili kushangaa).
Causative physical devastation — Hifil forms meaning to lay waste, destroy, or bring ruin upon a land, city, or people (Arabic أَخْرَبَ/يُخْرِبُ, Korean 황폐케 하다, Swahili kuharibu).

Agentive participle used substantivally for the one who causes desolation — Qal and Piel active participles functioning as nouns, including Daniel's 'abomination that makes desolate' (Arabic مُخَرِّبٌ, Korean 황폐케 하는 자, Swahili mwenye kuharibu).
Abstract nominal use via Hofal infinitive construct, denoting the condition or process of becoming desolate (Arabic الْخَرَابِ, Korean 황폐의, Swahili ukiwa).
Causative of the psychological sense — Hifil forms meaning to cause others to be appalled, stunned, or horrified (Arabic أُذْهِلُ/انْدَهِشُوا, Korean 놀라게 하다, Swahili kufanya kushangaa).
